RagShortTexts: The Council of Fifteen established by the Provisions of Oxford stripped Henry III of unchecked rule.

Variants.Content: The 1258 Provisions of Oxford placed King Henry III under the supervision of a representative Council of Fifteen chosen by barons. Convening thrice-yearly Parliaments, the council seized control over appointments of the chancellor, treasurer, and local sheriffs.

Simon de Montfort maintains that kings are bound by oath to their subjects and cannot squander treasury coin on foreign favourites. Barons sit in Westminster with swords at hand to seal every royal decree.
The lords in London argue whether the King is tyrant or the barons rebels. But whoever serves as sheriff, their tax measures never get any lighter for our village.
